nodes.text: Let $g(k)$ be the smallest integer (if any such exists) such that any $g(k)$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ contains an empty convex $k$-gon (i.e. with no point in the interior). Does $g(k)$ exist? If so, estimate $g(k)$.

#216 : [Er78c] [Er81] [Er82e] [Er83c] [Er97e] geometry | convex A variant of the 'happy ending' problem [107] , which asks for the same without the 'no point in the interior' restriction. Erdős observed $g(4)=5$ (as with the happy ending problem) but Harborth [Ha78] showed $g(5)=10$. Nicolás [Ni07] and Gerken [Ge08] independently showed that $g(6)$ exists. Horton [Ho83] showed that $g(n)$ does not exist for $n\geq 7$. Heule and Scheucher [HeSc24] have proved that $g(6)=30$. This problem is #2 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.
